author: NorthEast News Desk
body: China and India are arranging a bilateral meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, China’s foreign ministry said Friday. The talks would take place around the BRICS summit in New Delhi, where Xi is scheduled to join other leaders this weekend.

Foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Beijing is willing to approach relations with India from a strategic and long-term perspective, strengthen communication and cooperation, and manage differences. The statement did not provide a finalized time or agenda for the leaders’ meeting.

Xi is expected to address the BRICS gathering and hold broader exchanges with participating leaders about the international situation, according to the ministry. The summit gives China and India a multilateral setting for direct contact while both governments manage a relationship that combines substantial economic ties with persistent strategic disagreements.

The development remains fluid because officials said the bilateral meeting was being organized rather than announcing a completed schedule. Any outcome will depend on the talks themselves and on statements issued by the two governments afterward. The immediate confirmed development is that both sides are working toward leader-level discussions during Xi’s visit to India.
dek: China’s foreign ministry says the neighboring powers are organizing bilateral talks as President Xi Jinping travels to India for the weekend gathering.
headline: China and India arrange Xi-Modi meeting ahead of BRICS summit
